scenario.feature: Send email on the user's behalf; optionally read the inbox

summary.text: Google fully supports third-party OAuth 2.0 for server-side applications accessing the Gmail API.
Developers can register an OAuth app in Google Cloud by setting the consent screen to External or Internal user types.

Send-only integrations require https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send (sensitive scope, standard verification). Inbox reading requires https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly (restricted scope).

Handling restricted data on servers triggers an annual third-party Cloud Application Security Assessment (CASA Tier 2). A send-only integration avoids restricted scope review and security assessments.

next_action.instruction: Create a Google Cloud project and configure the OAuth consent screen with external user type.
next_action.success_condition: A Google Cloud project is created and the OAuth consent screen is configured.

paths.name: Testing & Development Mode
paths.applicability: Suitable for initial development and testing with up to 100 test users without immediate app verification.

gates.note: Not mandatory for initial testing using test users under the testing publishing status.

limits.text: Limited to up to 100 test users for apps in Testing publishing status.

steps.success_condition: OAuth client ID is created and test users are added.

waiting.explanation: No waiting period for testing setup.

paths.name: Production Deployment for External Customers
paths.applicability: Required when deploying the feature to external customers utilizing sensitive Gmail scopes.

gates.note: Required for external users requesting sensitive or restricted Gmail scopes.

Restricted scopes like gmail.readonly require an annual Cloud Application Security Assessment (CASA Tier 2) by an authorized third-party assessor when handling data on servers. Send-only access (gmail.send) is sensitive and requires only standard Google verification.
Restrictions apply on AI/ML model training using restricted scope user data without explicit consent.

prerequisites.text: Google Cloud project with OAuth consent screen set to External user type.
Compliance with Google API Services User Data Policy.

steps.title: Configure Production OAuth and Submit for Verification
steps.instructions: Implement server-side authorization flow and configure production OAuth credentials. Google states verification takes several weeks. As planning estimates: 2-3 weeks for standard sensitive verification (gmail.send); 4-8+ weeks if restricted inbox reading (gmail.readonly) requires third-party CASA Tier 2 security assessment.
steps.success_condition: Verification and security assessment submission are completed.

effort.explanation: Estimated effort to implement server-side flow and prepare verification submission materials.

waiting.explanation: Google notes verification takes several weeks. Planning estimates: 2 to 3 weeks for sensitive scope (gmail.send) verification; 4 to 8+ weeks when restricted scope (gmail.readonly) requires third-party CASA Tier 2 assessment.

scopes.purpose: Send email on the user's behalf

blockers.trigger: Requesting https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send for external customers without Google OAuth app verification
blockers.consequence: Unverified app consent warning displayed to external users, with access capped at 100 test users.
blockers.resolution: Submit the app for standard Google OAuth verification with a YouTube consent demo video, privacy policy, and verified domain (planning estimate: 2-3 weeks).

blockers.trigger: Requesting https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly for external customers when handling email data on servers
blockers.consequence: App blocked from production until an authorized third-party security lab completes an annual CASA Tier 2 security assessment.
blockers.resolution: If inbox reading is optional, omit gmail.readonly to avoid restricted scope requirements. If required, complete annual CASA Tier 2 assessment (planning estimate: 4-8+ weeks and assessor fee).

conflicts.topic: Precise classification and assessment triggers for `gmail.readonly` and `gmail.send`
conflicts.description: S1 states that `gmail.send` and `gmail.readonly` are sensitive and require a security assessment, whereas S2 classifies them under standard sensitive/restricted scope verification tracks.
conflicts.resolution: Both apply depending on whether Google classifies the particular deployment as requiring standard sensitive verification or a full CASA assessment; S1 reflects tighter enforcement of security assessments for external customer-facing apps requesting mailbox access.

claims.text: Third-party OAuth 2.0 is fully supported by Google for web, server-side, and installed applications accessing the Gmail API.
claims.conditions: When accessing Gmail API via web, server-side, or installed applications.

claims.text: Any developer with a Google Cloud account may register an OAuth app; registration requires creating a Google Cloud project, configuring the OAuth consent screen, and setting the user type to External or Internal.
claims.conditions: When registering an OAuth app in Google Cloud.

claims.text: Google classifies https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send as sensitive (Send email on your behalf) and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly as restricted (View your email messages and settings).
claims.conditions: When requesting permissions to send mail and read the inbox.

claims.text: For external customers, Google states that verification takes several weeks. As planning estimates: standard send-only verification (gmail.send) takes 2-3 weeks, whereas server-side handling of restricted data (gmail.readonly) requires a third-party CASA Tier 2 security assessment taking 4-8+ weeks.
claims.conditions: When requesting sensitive scopes for users outside the Google Workspace organization.
claims.support_note: Google documentation broadly states verification takes several weeks; specific 2-3 week and 4-8+ week durations are planning estimates for sensitive review and CASA Tier 2 assessment respectively.

claims.text: To get a first test connection working, a developer creates credentials in the Google Cloud Console, configures a test consent screen, and adds test users (up to 100 users for apps in Testing publishing status).
claims.conditions: When using apps in Testing publishing status.

claims.text: Your app needs Google OAuth app verification if it is set to External user type on the OAuth consent screen and requests any sensitive or restricted Gmail scopes from users outside your own Google Workspace organization.
claims.conditions: When app is set to External and requests sensitive or restricted scopes.
claims.excerpt: Your app needs Google OAuth app verification if it is set to External user type on the OAuth consent screen and requests any sensitive or restricted Gmail scopes from users outside your own Google Workspace organization.

claims.text: Google API Services User Data Policy mandates CASA Tier 2 security assessments for server-side restricted data handling and prohibits using restricted scope data to train generalized AI/ML models without affirmative user consent.
claims.conditions: When utilizing Google API services and restricted scopes.
claims.excerpt: Your application must follow Google’s API Services User Data Policy and meet additional requirements for specific scopes.

claims.conditions: When initiating development and verification submission.
